publish.title: Beat procrastination with a 25-minute timer
publish.description: The Pomodoro Technique in four steps.

scenes.headline: Beat procrastination with a timer
scenes.narration: Cannot start? Do not plan the whole afternoon. Plan twenty-five minutes.

scenes.headline: The method
scenes.narration: Pick one task, work for one interval of about twenty-five minutes, take a short break, then go again.

scenes.headline: Where it comes from
scenes.narration: Francesco Cirillo created the Pomodoro Technique in the late nineteen eighties, named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer.

scenes.headline: Why short bursts work
scenes.narration: A small, fixed block is easier to start than an open-ended afternoon, and the break is built in.

scenes.headline: Set a timer now
scenes.narration: Choose one task and start the clock.
